newsitem.title: JAPAN: Kuraray to build $85 mln resin plant in Belgium.
newsitem.headline: Kuraray to build $85 mln resin plant in Belgium.

text.p: Kuraray Co Ltd said on Thursday that it would invest about $85 million to build a plant in Belgium for the production of ethylene vinyl alcohol (EVOH) copolymer resins.
The plant, to be built in Antwerp, will have an annual production capacity of 10,000 tonnes, the Japanese synthetic fibre maker said in a statement.
The plant will start production in the autumn of 1999, Kuraray said.
EVOH copolymer resins are largely used for food packaging but are also used for fuel tanks in cars and other industrial products.
The Antwerp plant will be Kuraray's third EVOH plant, the company said, adding that it currently has a plant in Japan and another one in the United States.
When the new plant in Antwerp begins production, Kuraray's total worldwide capacity for EVOH resins will be 41,000 tonnes annually.
Kuraray decided to build the new plant to meet growing demand in the European market.

"By having a new manufacturing facility in Antwerp, Kuraray will be able to more quickly meet greater customer requirements in western Europe and also meet the needs of customers in the developing east European countries," Kuraray said.
Currently Kuraray supplies its European customers with EVOH copolymer resins from its Japanese and U.S. plants.
